# Camp Michaux and Sunset Rocks: History, Vistas and More in Michaux Forest, PA

Feb 17, 2020

Follow along with the Department of Adventure on a 3-mile journey to explore history, the Appalachian Trail, and beautiful vistas of Michaux State Forest. The adventure begins at the parking area at the intersection of Bunk Hill Road and Michaux Road, northwest of Pine Grove Furnace State Park.

![Image 4: Historic Barn Wall Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060759_grande.JPG?v=1513956748)

### Where to begin?

There are a few parking areas here, but we suggest the lot that sits directly in front of a historic crumbling barn wall (pictured above). From this parking area, we wanted to head east towards Halfway Spring and Sunset Rocks. We considered walking north on Michaux Road to intersect with the Appalachian Trail and then following this to Halfway Spring, but on this particular day we decided to follow a few short paths from this barn structure downhill to Bunker Hill Road. We then followed Bunker Hill Road, which is gravel and has very little car traffic, to a gate and intersection with the Appalachian Trail.

![Image 5: Appalachian Trail Toms Run Bridge Crossing Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060762_grande.JPG?v=1513957205)

We found the famous white blazes of the Appalachian Trail and turned right along the path towards Toms Run. The Appalachian Trail is easy to follow here, and includes a fun bridge crossing of Toms Run.

![Image 6: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060764_grande.JPG?v=1513957349)

### Sunset Rocks Trail

We quickly found Sunset Rocks trail after crossing Toms Run. The blue blazes on boulders acting as a barricade for the old road and the obvious trail sign, made this turn hard to miss. Sunset Rocks Trail was wide here before beginning to climbing gently uphill towards Little Rocky Ridge. The climb became a bit steeper as we gained the ridge, but we weren't deterred as we were excited for the upcoming vistas.

![Image 7: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060768_grande.JPG?v=1513957556)

### Little Rocky Ridge

The blue blazed trail leads up to a small saddle of Little Rocky Ridge. Our [Michaux Lizard Map](https://www.purplelizard.com/collections/maps/products/michaux-map "Michaux Map") highlights the trail heading east (right) toward Michaux Road, but explorers could also turn left (west) here for more vistas along Little Rocky Ridge. Blue blazes continue left for a while but eventually end. Exploring by foot is allowed anywhere along this ridge but be careful not to lose your way!

![Image 8: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060770_grande.JPG?v=1513958194)

Little Rocky Ridge is a wonderful place to explore with some steep cliffs along the edges of the ridge. Rogue the Adventure Pup is a bit too daring around these drop-offs and has a history of leaping into the great unknown, so she was secured to trees while we studied the rocky crags of the ridge.

![Image 9: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060771_grande.JPG?v=1513958362)

### Vistas Galore and Bouldering Delights!

There are several spectacular sweeping vistas that overlook Michaux State Forest and Pine Grove Furnace State Park to the southeast. Fall and winter offer some majestic viewsheds!

![Image 10: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060782_grande.JPG?v=1513958544)

This ridge is filled with large boulders that are ideal for scrambling and rock climbing. We attempted to climb a few of these rocks, even though most of our climbing skills were forgotten years ago. Want to find some brand new muscles? Grab a crag and Spiderman yourself on the rock face for a few seconds.

![Image 11: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060792_grande.JPG?v=1513958691)

Although this section of trail is only about a mile long, it can be a bit slow going because of all the rock hopping. Most of the steep rock crags can be bypassed by those who aren't comfortable rock scrambling. With that said, small children and pets may need to be carried or hoisted around some of the larger boulders.

![Image 12: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060796_grande.JPG?v=1513958896)

The rocky ridgeline disappears and the trail mellows out again as it descends toward Michaux Road. The trail winds around a leased camp and then shares a dirt driveway until it exits onto Michaux Road. We turned north (right) on Michaux Road and headed back to our parking area.

### Choices

Those who want to experience more of the Appalachian Trail and an Appalachian Trail Shelter Area, can reference the Michaux Lizard Map and follow the west section of Sunset Rocks Trail which leads to Toms Run Shelter. From here head north on the AT until it crosses Michaux Road again, then simply road walk back to your parking area. This alternative route adds about 3 miles to the loop described above.

![Image 13: Michaux Camp Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060804_grande.JPG?v=1513959243)

Before we jumped back in our car, we visited the site of Camp Michaux, which surrounded our parking spot. This area has just too much history to fit on our Lizard Map, but thankfully the [Cumberland Valley Historical Society](https://www.historicalsociety.com/) offers a [self-guided walking tour sheet](https://www.historicalsociety.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/CampMichauxInteriorWeb.pdf "Camp Michaux Walking Tour Michaux State Forest PA") that depicts all of the history that occurred on this site.

![Image 14: Appalachian Trail Museum Pine Grove Furnace State Park Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1040892_grande.JPG?v=1513960209)

History buffs and Appalachian Trail enthusiasts will want to stop at the Appalachian Trail Museum in Pine Grove Furnace State Park on the drive home. The museum is open seasonally beginning in April every spring. Call ahead to check hours of operation.

**Explore all Michaux has to offer!**

# Camp Michaux and Sunset Rocks: History, Vistas and More in Michaux Forest, PA

Feb 17, 2020

Follow along with the Department of Adventure on a 3-mile journey to explore history, the Appalachian Trail, and beautiful vistas of Michaux State Forest. The adventure begins at the parking area at the intersection of Bunk Hill Road and Michaux Road, northwest of Pine Grove Furnace State Park.

![Image 4: Historic Barn Wall Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060759_grande.JPG?v=1513956748)

### Where to begin?

There are a few parking areas here, but we suggest the lot that sits directly in front of a historic crumbling barn wall (pictured above). From this parking area, we wanted to head east towards Halfway Spring and Sunset Rocks. We considered walking north on Michaux Road to intersect with the Appalachian Trail and then following this to Halfway Spring, but on this particular day we decided to follow a few short paths from this barn structure downhill to Bunker Hill Road. We then followed Bunker Hill Road, which is gravel and has very little car traffic, to a gate and intersection with the Appalachian Trail.

![Image 5: Appalachian Trail Toms Run Bridge Crossing Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060762_grande.JPG?v=1513957205)

We found the famous white blazes of the Appalachian Trail and turned right along the path towards Toms Run. The Appalachian Trail is easy to follow here, and includes a fun bridge crossing of Toms Run.

![Image 6: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060764_grande.JPG?v=1513957349)

### Sunset Rocks Trail

We quickly found Sunset Rocks trail after crossing Toms Run. The blue blazes on boulders acting as a barricade for the old road and the obvious trail sign, made this turn hard to miss. Sunset Rocks Trail was wide here before beginning to climbing gently uphill towards Little Rocky Ridge. The climb became a bit steeper as we gained the ridge, but we weren't deterred as we were excited for the upcoming vistas.

![Image 7: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060768_grande.JPG?v=1513957556)

### Little Rocky Ridge

The blue blazed trail leads up to a small saddle of Little Rocky Ridge. Our [Michaux Lizard Map](https://www.purplelizard.com/collections/maps/products/michaux-map "Michaux Map") highlights the trail heading east (right) toward Michaux Road, but explorers could also turn left (west) here for more vistas along Little Rocky Ridge. Blue blazes continue left for a while but eventually end. Exploring by foot is allowed anywhere along this ridge but be careful not to lose your way!

![Image 8: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060770_grande.JPG?v=1513958194)

Little Rocky Ridge is a wonderful place to explore with some steep cliffs along the edges of the ridge. Rogue the Adventure Pup is a bit too daring around these drop-offs and has a history of leaping into the great unknown, so she was secured to trees while we studied the rocky crags of the ridge.

![Image 9: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060771_grande.JPG?v=1513958362)

### Vistas Galore and Bouldering Delights!

There are several spectacular sweeping vistas that overlook Michaux State Forest and Pine Grove Furnace State Park to the southeast. Fall and winter offer some majestic viewsheds!

![Image 10: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060782_grande.JPG?v=1513958544)

This ridge is filled with large boulders that are ideal for scrambling and rock climbing. We attempted to climb a few of these rocks, even though most of our climbing skills were forgotten years ago. Want to find some brand new muscles? Grab a crag and Spiderman yourself on the rock face for a few seconds.

![Image 11: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060792_grande.JPG?v=1513958691)

Although this section of trail is only about a mile long, it can be a bit slow going because of all the rock hopping. Most of the steep rock crags can be bypassed by those who aren't comfortable rock scrambling. With that said, small children and pets may need to be carried or hoisted around some of the larger boulders.

![Image 12: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060796_grande.JPG?v=1513958896)

The rocky ridgeline disappears and the trail mellows out again as it descends toward Michaux Road. The trail winds around a leased camp and then shares a dirt driveway until it exits onto Michaux Road. We turned north (right) on Michaux Road and headed back to our parking area.

### Choices

Those who want to experience more of the Appalachian Trail and an Appalachian Trail Shelter Area, can reference the Michaux Lizard Map and follow the west section of Sunset Rocks Trail which leads to Toms Run Shelter. From here head north on the AT until it crosses Michaux Road again, then simply road walk back to your parking area. This alternative route adds about 3 miles to the loop described above.

![Image 13: Michaux Camp Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060804_grande.JPG?v=1513959243)

Before we jumped back in our car, we visited the site of Camp Michaux, which surrounded our parking spot. This area has just too much history to fit on our Lizard Map, but thankfully the [Cumberland Valley Historical Society](https://www.historicalsociety.com/) offers a [self-guided walking tour sheet](https://www.historicalsociety.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/CampMichauxInteriorWeb.pdf "Camp Michaux Walking Tour Michaux State Forest PA") that depicts all of the history that occurred on this site.

![Image 14: Appalachian Trail Museum Pine Grove Furnace State Park Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1040892_grande.JPG?v=1513960209)

History buffs and Appalachian Trail enthusiasts will want to stop at the Appalachian Trail Museum in Pine Grove Furnace State Park on the drive home. The museum is open seasonally beginning in April every spring. Call ahead to check hours of operation.

# Camp Michaux and Sunset Rocks: History, Vistas and More in Michaux Forest, PA

Feb 17, 2020

Follow along with the Department of Adventure on a 3-mile journey to explore history, the Appalachian Trail, and beautiful vistas of Michaux State Forest. The adventure begins at the parking area at the intersection of Bunk Hill Road and Michaux Road, northwest of Pine Grove Furnace State Park.

![Image 4: Historic Barn Wall Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060759_grande.JPG?v=1513956748)

### Where to begin?

There are a few parking areas here, but we suggest the lot that sits directly in front of a historic crumbling barn wall (pictured above). From this parking area, we wanted to head east towards Halfway Spring and Sunset Rocks. We considered walking north on Michaux Road to intersect with the Appalachian Trail and then following this to Halfway Spring, but on this particular day we decided to follow a few short paths from this barn structure downhill to Bunker Hill Road. We then followed Bunker Hill Road, which is gravel and has very little car traffic, to a gate and intersection with the Appalachian Trail.

![Image 5: Appalachian Trail Toms Run Bridge Crossing Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060762_grande.JPG?v=1513957205)

We found the famous white blazes of the Appalachian Trail and turned right along the path towards Toms Run. The Appalachian Trail is easy to follow here, and includes a fun bridge crossing of Toms Run.

![Image 6: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060764_grande.JPG?v=1513957349)

### Sunset Rocks Trail

We quickly found Sunset Rocks trail after crossing Toms Run. The blue blazes on boulders acting as a barricade for the old road and the obvious trail sign, made this turn hard to miss. Sunset Rocks Trail was wide here before beginning to climbing gently uphill towards Little Rocky Ridge. The climb became a bit steeper as we gained the ridge, but we weren't deterred as we were excited for the upcoming vistas.

![Image 7: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060768_grande.JPG?v=1513957556)

### Little Rocky Ridge

The blue blazed trail leads up to a small saddle of Little Rocky Ridge. Our [Michaux Lizard Map](https://www.purplelizard.com/collections/maps/products/michaux-map "Michaux Map") highlights the trail heading east (right) toward Michaux Road, but explorers could also turn left (west) here for more vistas along Little Rocky Ridge. Blue blazes continue left for a while but eventually end. Exploring by foot is allowed anywhere along this ridge but be careful not to lose your way!

![Image 8: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060770_grande.JPG?v=1513958194)

Little Rocky Ridge is a wonderful place to explore with some steep cliffs along the edges of the ridge. Rogue the Adventure Pup is a bit too daring around these drop-offs and has a history of leaping into the great unknown, so she was secured to trees while we studied the rocky crags of the ridge.

![Image 9: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060771_grande.JPG?v=1513958362)

### Vistas Galore and Bouldering Delights!

There are several spectacular sweeping vistas that overlook Michaux State Forest and Pine Grove Furnace State Park to the southeast. Fall and winter offer some majestic viewsheds!

![Image 10: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060782_grande.JPG?v=1513958544)

This ridge is filled with large boulders that are ideal for scrambling and rock climbing. We attempted to climb a few of these rocks, even though most of our climbing skills were forgotten years ago. Want to find some brand new muscles? Grab a crag and Spiderman yourself on the rock face for a few seconds.

![Image 11: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060792_grande.JPG?v=1513958691)

Although this section of trail is only about a mile long, it can be a bit slow going because of all the rock hopping. Most of the steep rock crags can be bypassed by those who aren't comfortable rock scrambling. With that said, small children and pets may need to be carried or hoisted around some of the larger boulders.

![Image 12: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060796_grande.JPG?v=1513958896)

The rocky ridgeline disappears and the trail mellows out again as it descends toward Michaux Road. The trail winds around a leased camp and then shares a dirt driveway until it exits onto Michaux Road. We turned north (right) on Michaux Road and headed back to our parking area.

### Choices

Those who want to experience more of the Appalachian Trail and an Appalachian Trail Shelter Area, can reference the Michaux Lizard Map and follow the west section of Sunset Rocks Trail which leads to Toms Run Shelter. From here head north on the AT until it crosses Michaux Road again, then simply road walk back to your parking area. This alternative route adds about 3 miles to the loop described above.

![Image 13: Michaux Camp Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060804_grande.JPG?v=1513959243)

Before we jumped back in our car, we visited the site of Camp Michaux, which surrounded our parking spot. This area has just too much history to fit on our Lizard Map, but thankfully the [Cumberland Valley Historical Society](https://www.historicalsociety.com/) offers a self-guided walking tour sheet that depicts all of the history that occurred on this site.

![Image 14: Appalachian Trail Museum Pine Grove Furnace State Park Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1040892_grande.JPG?v=1513960209)

History buffs and Appalachian Trail enthusiasts will want to stop at the Appalachian Trail Museum in Pine Grove Furnace State Park on the drive home. The museum is open seasonally beginning in April every spring. Call ahead to check hours of operation.

# Camp Michaux and Sunset Rocks: History, Vistas and More in Michaux Forest, PA

Feb 17, 2020

Follow along with the Department of Adventure on a 3-mile journey to explore history, the Appalachian Trail, and beautiful vistas of Michaux State Forest. The adventure begins at the parking area at the intersection of Bunk Hill Road and Michaux Road, northwest of Pine Grove Furnace State Park.

![Image 4: Historic Barn Wall Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060759_grande.JPG?v=1513956748)

### Where to begin?

There are a few parking areas here, but we suggest the lot that sits directly in front of a historic crumbling barn wall (pictured above). From this parking area, we wanted to head east towards Halfway Spring and Sunset Rocks. We considered walking north on Michaux Road to intersect with the Appalachian Trail and then following this to Halfway Spring, but on this particular day we decided to follow a few short paths from this barn structure downhill to Bunker Hill Road. We then followed Bunker Hill Road, which is gravel and has very little car traffic, to a gate and intersection with the Appalachian Trail.

![Image 5: Appalachian Trail Toms Run Bridge Crossing Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060762_grande.JPG?v=1513957205)

We found the famous white blazes of the Appalachian Trail and turned right along the path towards Toms Run. The Appalachian Trail is easy to follow here, and includes a fun bridge crossing of Toms Run.

![Image 6: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060764_grande.JPG?v=1513957349)

### Sunset Rocks Trail

We quickly found Sunset Rocks trail after crossing Toms Run. The blue blazes on boulders acting as a barricade for the old road and the obvious trail sign, made this turn hard to miss. Sunset Rocks Trail was wide here before beginning to climbing gently uphill towards Little Rocky Ridge. The climb became a bit steeper as we gained the ridge, but we weren't deterred as we were excited for the upcoming vistas.

![Image 7: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060768_grande.JPG?v=1513957556)

### Little Rocky Ridge

The blue blazed trail leads up to a small saddle of Little Rocky Ridge. Our [Michaux Lizard Map](https://www.purplelizard.com/collections/maps/products/michaux-map "Michaux Map") highlights the trail heading east (right) toward Michaux Road, but explorers could also turn left (west) here for more vistas along Little Rocky Ridge. Blue blazes continue left for a while but eventually end. Exploring by foot is allowed anywhere along this ridge but be careful not to lose your way!

![Image 8: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060770_grande.JPG?v=1513958194)

Little Rocky Ridge is a wonderful place to explore with some steep cliffs along the edges of the ridge. Rogue the Adventure Pup is a bit too daring around these drop-offs and has a history of leaping into the great unknown, so she was secured to trees while we studied the rocky crags of the ridge.

![Image 9: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060771_grande.JPG?v=1513958362)

### Vistas Galore and Bouldering Delights!

There are several spectacular sweeping vistas that overlook Michaux State Forest and Pine Grove Furnace State Park to the southeast. Fall and winter offer some majestic viewsheds!

![Image 10: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060782_grande.JPG?v=1513958544)

This ridge is filled with large boulders that are ideal for scrambling and rock climbing. We attempted to climb a few of these rocks, even though most of our climbing skills were forgotten years ago. Want to find some brand new muscles? Grab a crag and Spiderman yourself on the rock face for a few seconds.

![Image 11: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060792_grande.JPG?v=1513958691)

Although this section of trail is only about a mile long, it can be a bit slow going because of all the rock hopping. Most of the steep rock crags can be bypassed by those who aren't comfortable rock scrambling. With that said, small children and pets may need to be carried or hoisted around some of the larger boulders.

![Image 12: Sunset Rocks Trail Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060796_grande.JPG?v=1513958896)

The rocky ridgeline disappears and the trail mellows out again as it descends toward Michaux Road. The trail winds around a leased camp and then shares a dirt driveway until it exits onto Michaux Road. We turned north (right) on Michaux Road and headed back to our parking area.

### Choices

Those who want to experience more of the Appalachian Trail and an Appalachian Trail Shelter Area, can reference the Michaux Lizard Map and follow the west section of Sunset Rocks Trail which leads to Toms Run Shelter. From here head north on the AT until it crosses Michaux Road again, then simply road walk back to your parking area. This alternative route adds about 3 miles to the loop described above.

![Image 13: Michaux Camp Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1060804_grande.JPG?v=1513959243)

Before we jumped back in our car, we visited the site of Camp Michaux, which surrounded our parking spot. This area has just too much history to fit on our Lizard Map, but thankfully the [Cumberland Valley Historical Society](https://www.historicalsociety.com/) offers a self-guided walking tour sheet that depicts all of the history that occurred on this site.

![Image 14: Appalachian Trail Museum Pine Grove Furnace State Park Michaux State Forest PA](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0083/1372/files/P1040892_grande.JPG?v=1513960209)

History buffs and Appalachian Trail enthusiasts will want to stop at the Appalachian Trail Museum in Pine Grove Furnace State Park on the drive home. The museum is open seasonally beginning in April every spring. Call ahead to check hours of operation.

**Explore all Michaux has to offer!**

Hiking in Michaux State Forest offers diverse landscapes across its approximately 85,000 acres, characterized by rolling hillsides and forested ridgelines that mark the transition from the Blue Ridge to the Allegheny Mountains. The forest features numerous water bodies, including ponds, lakes, reservoirs like Long Pine Run Reservoir, and natural trout streams such as Conococheague Creek. Its second-growth forest habitat includes thick rhododendron pockets, tall pines, and mixed oaks, providing varied terrain for easy hiking trails.

## Frequently Asked Questions

How many easy hiking trails are available in Michaux State Forest?
Michaux State Forest offers a good selection of easy hiking trails, with _11 routes_ specifically categorized as easy. In total, there are 38 hiking tours available across various difficulty levels.

What kind of terrain can I expect on easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Easy hikes in Michaux State Forest typically feature rolling hillsides and forested ridgelines, characteristic of the Blue Ridge Mountains transitioning into the Alleghenies. You'll find paths through thick rhododendron pockets, tall pines, and mixed oak forests, often alongside natural trout streams and reservoirs. The trails are generally well-maintained, providing a pleasant walking experience.

Are there easy trails with scenic viewpoints in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, several easy trails lead to rewarding scenic viewpoints. For instance, the [Pole Steeple Trail](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813343279/pole-steeple-trail), though it has some elevation gain, offers expansive westward views from the Pole Steeple Overlook. Another option is [Sunset Rocks from Old Shippenburg Road](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813360303/sunset-rocks-from-old-shippenburg-road), which provides panoramic views after a shorter hike.

What are some short, easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
For a quick and easy outing, consider the [Sunset Rocks from Old Shippenburg Road](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813360303/sunset-rocks-from-old-shippenburg-road) route, which is less than a mile long. Another short option is the [Appalachian Trail: Pine Grove Furnace to Tom's Run](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813348929/appalachian-trail-pine-grove-furnace-to-tom-s-run), an easy 1.4-mile path with gentle gradients.

Are there any easy loop trails in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, Michaux State Forest offers easy loop trails. The Hosack Run Loop is a scenic 4.2-mile option that takes you through rhododendron thickets and along mountain streams, utilizing a portion of the Appalachian Trail. While not in our guide data, the Long Pine Run Reservoir loop is another moderate 4.8-mile path in the area.

Can I bring my dog on easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, dogs are generally permitted on trails within Michaux State Forest. However, they must be kept on a leash at all times to ensure their safety and the comfort of other hikers and wildlife. Always remember to pack out any waste.

Are there family-friendly easy trails in Michaux State Forest?
Many of the easy trails in Michaux State Forest are suitable for families. Their gentle gradients and manageable distances make them ideal for children and those looking for a relaxed outdoor experience. The varied forest habitat and natural features provide engaging scenery for all ages.

What natural features or landmarks can I see on easy trails?
Michaux State Forest is rich in natural features and landmarks. Along easy trails, you might encounter serene water bodies like the Long Pine Run Reservoir or natural trout streams. Notable attractions include the [Laurel Lake](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/4816643), and historical sites like [Camp Michaux](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/4025592). The forest itself, with its second-growth pines, oaks, and rhododendron, is a beautiful feature.

What is the best time of year for easy hiking in Michaux State Forest?
Spring and fall are generally considered the best times for easy hiking in Michaux State Forest. Spring brings blooming wildflowers and lush greenery, while fall offers spectacular foliage. Summer can be pleasant, but be prepared for warmer temperatures and potential humidity. Winter hiking is also possible, though some trails may be icy or covered in snow.

Where can I park for easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Michaux State Forest provides numerous parking areas and access points for its trails. Many trailheads, especially those near popular routes like the Appalachian Trail sections or viewpoints, have designated parking lots. Additionally, the state parks within the forest, such as Pine Grove Furnace State Park, offer amenities including parking that can serve as starting points for hikes.

Is public transport available to Michaux State Forest?
Direct public transport options to Michaux State Forest are limited. Visitors typically access the forest by car, as it spans a large rural area. Planning your trip with personal transportation will offer the most flexibility for reaching various trailheads and attractions.

What do other hikers say about the easy trails in Michaux State Forest?
The easy trails in Michaux State Forest are highly regarded by the komoot community, with an average rating of **4.8 stars** from over 20 reviews. Hikers often praise the peaceful forest environment, the well-marked paths, and the rewarding views from spots like Pole Steeple. Many appreciate the diverse landscapes and the opportunity to experience sections of the iconic Appalachian Trail.

Are there any specific regulations or permits required for hiking in Michaux State Forest?
Generally, no permits are required for day hiking on the established trails in Michaux State Forest. However, it's always a good practice to familiarize yourself with the Pennsylvania DCNR State Forest rules and regulations, especially regarding camping, fires, or specific activities. You can find more information on the official [PA DCNR website](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dcnr/recreation/where-to-go/state-forests/find-a-forest/michaux/hiking).

Hiking in Michaux State Forest offers diverse landscapes across its approximately 85,000 acres, characterized by rolling hillsides and forested ridgelines that mark the transition from the Blue Ridge to the Allegheny Mountains. The forest features numerous water bodies, including ponds, lakes, reservoirs like Long Pine Run Reservoir, and natural trout streams such as Conococheague Creek. Its second-growth forest habitat includes thick rhododendron pockets, tall pines, and mixed oaks, providing varied terrain for easy hiking trails.

## Frequently Asked Questions

How many easy hiking trails are available in Michaux State Forest?
Michaux State Forest offers a good selection of easy hiking trails, with _11 routes_ specifically categorized as easy. In total, there are 38 hiking tours available across various difficulty levels.

What kind of terrain can I expect on easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Easy hikes in Michaux State Forest typically feature rolling hillsides and forested ridgelines, characteristic of the Blue Ridge Mountains transitioning into the Alleghenies. You'll find paths through thick rhododendron pockets, tall pines, and mixed oak forests, often alongside natural trout streams and reservoirs. The trails are generally well-maintained, providing a pleasant walking experience.

Are there easy trails with scenic viewpoints in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, several easy trails lead to rewarding scenic viewpoints. For instance, the [Pole Steeple Trail](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813343279/pole-steeple-trail), though it has some elevation gain, offers expansive westward views from the Pole Steeple Overlook. Another option is [Sunset Rocks from Old Shippenburg Road](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813360303/sunset-rocks-from-old-shippenburg-road), which provides panoramic views after a shorter hike.

What are some short, easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
For a quick and easy outing, consider the [Sunset Rocks from Old Shippenburg Road](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813360303/sunset-rocks-from-old-shippenburg-road) route, which is less than a mile long. Another short option is the [Appalachian Trail: Pine Grove Furnace to Tom's Run](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813348929/appalachian-trail-pine-grove-furnace-to-tom-s-run), an easy 1.4-mile path with gentle gradients.

Are there any easy loop trails in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, Michaux State Forest offers easy loop trails. The Hosack Run Loop is a scenic 4.2-mile option that takes you through rhododendron thickets and along mountain streams, utilizing a portion of the Appalachian Trail. While not in our guide data, the Long Pine Run Reservoir loop is another moderate 4.8-mile path in the area.

Can I bring my dog on easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, dogs are generally permitted on trails within Michaux State Forest. However, they must be kept on a leash at all times to ensure their safety and the comfort of other hikers and wildlife. Always remember to pack out any waste.

Are there family-friendly easy trails in Michaux State Forest?
Many of the easy trails in Michaux State Forest are suitable for families. Their gentle gradients and manageable distances make them ideal for children and those looking for a relaxed outdoor experience. The varied forest habitat and natural features provide engaging scenery for all ages.

What natural features or landmarks can I see on easy trails?
Michaux State Forest is rich in natural features and landmarks. Along easy trails, you might encounter serene water bodies like the Long Pine Run Reservoir or natural trout streams. Notable attractions include the [Laurel Lake](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/4816643), and historical sites like [Camp Michaux](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/4025592). The forest itself, with its second-growth pines, oaks, and rhododendron, is a beautiful feature.

What is the best time of year for easy hiking in Michaux State Forest?
Spring and fall are generally considered the best times for easy hiking in Michaux State Forest. Spring brings blooming wildflowers and lush greenery, while fall offers spectacular foliage. Summer can be pleasant, but be prepared for warmer temperatures and potential humidity. Winter hiking is also possible, though some trails may be icy or covered in snow.

Where can I park for easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Michaux State Forest provides numerous parking areas and access points for its trails. Many trailheads, especially those near popular routes like the Appalachian Trail sections or viewpoints, have designated parking lots. Additionally, the state parks within the forest, such as Pine Grove Furnace State Park, offer amenities including parking that can serve as starting points for hikes.

Is public transport available to Michaux State Forest?
Direct public transport options to Michaux State Forest are limited. Visitors typically access the forest by car, as it spans a large rural area. Planning your trip with personal transportation will offer the most flexibility for reaching various trailheads and attractions.

What do other hikers say about the easy trails in Michaux State Forest?
The easy trails in Michaux State Forest are highly regarded by the komoot community, with an average rating of **4.8 stars** from over 20 reviews. Hikers often praise the peaceful forest environment, the well-marked paths, and the rewarding views from spots like Pole Steeple. Many appreciate the diverse landscapes and the opportunity to experience sections of the iconic Appalachian Trail.

Are there any specific regulations or permits required for hiking in Michaux State Forest?
Generally, no permits are required for day hiking on the established trails in Michaux State Forest. However, it's always a good practice to familiarize yourself with the Pennsylvania DCNR State Forest rules and regulations, especially regarding camping, fires, or specific activities. You can find more information on the official [PA DCNR website](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dcnr/recreation/where-to-go/state-forests/find-a-forest/michaux/hiking).

Hiking in Michaux State Forest offers diverse landscapes across its approximately 85,000 acres, characterized by rolling hillsides and forested ridgelines that mark the transition from the Blue Ridge to the Allegheny Mountains. The forest features numerous water bodies, including ponds, lakes, reservoirs like Long Pine Run Reservoir, and natural trout streams such as Conococheague Creek. Its second-growth forest habitat includes thick rhododendron pockets, tall pines, and mixed oaks, providing varied terrain for easy hiking trails.

## Frequently Asked Questions

How many easy hiking trails are available in Michaux State Forest?
Michaux State Forest offers a good selection of easy hiking trails, with _11 routes_ specifically categorized as easy. In total, there are 38 hiking tours available across various difficulty levels.

What kind of terrain can I expect on easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Easy hikes in Michaux State Forest typically feature rolling hillsides and forested ridgelines, characteristic of the Blue Ridge Mountains transitioning into the Alleghenies. You'll find paths through thick rhododendron pockets, tall pines, and mixed oak forests, often alongside natural trout streams and reservoirs. The trails are generally well-maintained, providing a pleasant walking experience.

Are there easy trails with scenic viewpoints in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, several easy trails lead to rewarding scenic viewpoints. For instance, the [Pole Steeple Trail](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813343279/pole-steeple-trail), though it has some elevation gain, offers expansive westward views from the Pole Steeple Overlook. Another option is [Sunset Rocks from Old Shippenburg Road](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813360303/sunset-rocks-from-old-shippenburg-road), which provides panoramic views after a shorter hike.

What are some short, easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
For a quick and easy outing, consider the [Sunset Rocks from Old Shippenburg Road](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813360303/sunset-rocks-from-old-shippenburg-road) route, which is less than a mile long. Another short option is the [Appalachian Trail: Pine Grove Furnace to Tom's Run](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813348929/appalachian-trail-pine-grove-furnace-to-tom-s-run), an easy 1.4-mile path with gentle gradients.

Are there any easy loop trails in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, Michaux State Forest offers easy loop trails. The Hosack Run Loop is a scenic 4.2-mile option that takes you through rhododendron thickets and along mountain streams, utilizing a portion of the Appalachian Trail. While not in our guide data, the Long Pine Run Reservoir loop is another moderate 4.8-mile path in the area.

Can I bring my dog on easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, dogs are generally permitted on trails within Michaux State Forest. However, they must be kept on a leash at all times to ensure their safety and the comfort of other hikers and wildlife. Always remember to pack out any waste.

Are there family-friendly easy trails in Michaux State Forest?
Many of the easy trails in Michaux State Forest are suitable for families. Their gentle gradients and manageable distances make them ideal for children and those looking for a relaxed outdoor experience. The varied forest habitat and natural features provide engaging scenery for all ages.

What natural features or landmarks can I see on easy trails?
Michaux State Forest is rich in natural features and landmarks. Along easy trails, you might encounter serene water bodies like the Long Pine Run Reservoir or natural trout streams. Notable attractions include the [Laurel Lake](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/4816643), and historical sites like [Camp Michaux](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/4025592). The forest itself, with its second-growth pines, oaks, and rhododendron, is a beautiful feature.

What is the best time of year for easy hiking in Michaux State Forest?
Spring and fall are generally considered the best times for easy hiking in Michaux State Forest. Spring brings blooming wildflowers and lush greenery, while fall offers spectacular foliage. Summer can be pleasant, but be prepared for warmer temperatures and potential humidity. Winter hiking is also possible, though some trails may be icy or covered in snow.

Where can I park for easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Michaux State Forest provides numerous parking areas and access points for its trails. Many trailheads, especially those near popular routes like the Appalachian Trail sections or viewpoints, have designated parking lots. Additionally, the state parks within the forest, such as Pine Grove Furnace State Park, offer amenities including parking that can serve as starting points for hikes.

Is public transport available to Michaux State Forest?
Direct public transport options to Michaux State Forest are limited. Visitors typically access the forest by car, as it spans a large rural area. Planning your trip with personal transportation will offer the most flexibility for reaching various trailheads and attractions.

What do other hikers say about the easy trails in Michaux State Forest?
The easy trails in Michaux State Forest are highly regarded by the komoot community, with an average rating of **4.8 stars** from over 20 reviews. Hikers often praise the peaceful forest environment, the well-marked paths, and the rewarding views from spots like Pole Steeple. Many appreciate the diverse landscapes and the opportunity to experience sections of the iconic Appalachian Trail.

Are there any specific regulations or permits required for hiking in Michaux State Forest?
Generally, no permits are required for day hiking on the established trails in Michaux State Forest. However, it's always a good practice to familiarize yourself with the Pennsylvania DCNR State Forest rules and regulations, especially regarding camping, fires, or specific activities. You can find more information on the official [PA DCNR website](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dcnr/recreation/where-to-go/state-forests/find-a-forest/michaux/hiking).

Hiking in Michaux State Forest offers diverse landscapes across its approximately 85,000 acres, characterized by rolling hillsides and forested ridgelines that mark the transition from the Blue Ridge to the Allegheny Mountains. The forest features numerous water bodies, including ponds, lakes, reservoirs like Long Pine Run Reservoir, and natural trout streams such as Conococheague Creek. Its second-growth forest habitat includes thick rhododendron pockets, tall pines, and mixed oaks, providing varied terrain for easy hiking trails.

## Frequently Asked Questions

How many easy hiking trails are available in Michaux State Forest?
Michaux State Forest offers a good selection of easy hiking trails, with _11 routes_ specifically categorized as easy. In total, there are 38 hiking tours available across various difficulty levels.

What kind of terrain can I expect on easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Easy hikes in Michaux State Forest typically feature rolling hillsides and forested ridgelines, characteristic of the Blue Ridge Mountains transitioning into the Alleghenies. You'll find paths through thick rhododendron pockets, tall pines, and mixed oak forests, often alongside natural trout streams and reservoirs. The trails are generally well-maintained, providing a pleasant walking experience.

Are there easy trails with scenic viewpoints in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, several easy trails lead to rewarding scenic viewpoints. For instance, the [Pole Steeple Trail](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813343279/pole-steeple-trail), though it has some elevation gain, offers expansive westward views from the Pole Steeple Overlook. Another option is [Sunset Rocks from Old Shippenburg Road](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813360303/sunset-rocks-from-old-shippenburg-road), which provides panoramic views after a shorter hike.

What are some short, easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
For a quick and easy outing, consider the [Sunset Rocks from Old Shippenburg Road](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813360303/sunset-rocks-from-old-shippenburg-road) route, which is less than a mile long. Another short option is the [Appalachian Trail: Pine Grove Furnace to Tom's Run](https://www.komoot.com/smarttour/e2813348929/appalachian-trail-pine-grove-furnace-to-tom-s-run), an easy 1.4-mile path with gentle gradients.

Are there any easy loop trails in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, Michaux State Forest offers easy loop trails. The Hosack Run Loop is a scenic 4.2-mile option that takes you through rhododendron thickets and along mountain streams, utilizing a portion of the Appalachian Trail. While not in our guide data, the Long Pine Run Reservoir loop is another moderate 4.8-mile path in the area.

Can I bring my dog on easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Yes, dogs are generally permitted on trails within Michaux State Forest. However, they must be kept on a leash at all times to ensure their safety and the comfort of other hikers and wildlife. Always remember to pack out any waste.

Are there family-friendly easy trails in Michaux State Forest?
Many of the easy trails in Michaux State Forest are suitable for families. Their gentle gradients and manageable distances make them ideal for children and those looking for a relaxed outdoor experience. The varied forest habitat and natural features provide engaging scenery for all ages.

What natural features or landmarks can I see on easy trails?
Michaux State Forest is rich in natural features and landmarks. Along easy trails, you might encounter serene water bodies like the Long Pine Run Reservoir or natural trout streams. Notable attractions include the [Laurel Lake](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/4816643), and historical sites like [Camp Michaux](https://www.komoot.com/highlight/4025592). The forest itself, with its second-growth pines, oaks, and rhododendron, is a beautiful feature.

What is the best time of year for easy hiking in Michaux State Forest?
Spring and fall are generally considered the best times for easy hiking in Michaux State Forest. Spring brings blooming wildflowers and lush greenery, while fall offers spectacular foliage. Summer can be pleasant, but be prepared for warmer temperatures and potential humidity. Winter hiking is also possible, though some trails may be icy or covered in snow.

Where can I park for easy hikes in Michaux State Forest?
Michaux State Forest provides numerous parking areas and access points for its trails. Many trailheads, especially those near popular routes like the Appalachian Trail sections or viewpoints, have designated parking lots. Additionally, the state parks within the forest, such as Pine Grove Furnace State Park, offer amenities including parking that can serve as starting points for hikes.

Is public transport available to Michaux State Forest?
Direct public transport options to Michaux State Forest are limited. Visitors typically access the forest by car, as it spans a large rural area. Planning your trip with personal transportation will offer the most flexibility for reaching various trailheads and attractions.

What do other hikers say about the easy trails in Michaux State Forest?
The easy trails in Michaux State Forest are highly regarded by the komoot community, with an average rating of **4.8 stars** from over 20 reviews. Hikers often praise the peaceful forest environment, the well-marked paths, and the rewarding views from spots like Pole Steeple. Many appreciate the diverse landscapes and the opportunity to experience sections of the iconic Appalachian Trail.

Are there any specific regulations or permits required for hiking in Michaux State Forest?
Generally, no permits are required for day hiking on the established trails in Michaux State Forest. However, it's always a good practice to familiarize yourself with the Pennsylvania DCNR State Forest rules and regulations, especially regarding camping, fires, or specific activities. You can find more information on the official [PA DCNR website](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dcnr/recreation/where-to-go/state-forests/find-a-forest/michaux/hiking).

**Susquehanna County** is a [county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States) "County (United States)") in the [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_(U.S._state) "Commonwealth (U.S. state)") of [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the population was 38,434[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-QF-2) Its [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") is [Montrose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montrose,_Pennsylvania "Montrose, Pennsylvania").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-GR6-3) The county was created on February 21, 1810, from part of [Luzerne County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzerne_County,_Pennsylvania "Luzerne County, Pennsylvania")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-4) and later organized in 1812.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-5) It is named for the [Susquehanna River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_River "Susquehanna River"). The county is part of the [Northeast Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeastern_Pennsylvania "Northeastern Pennsylvania") region of the state.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-6)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Settlement and conflict

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Settlement and conflict")]

The first non-[Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_people "Indigenous people") settlers began to move into the area from Philadelphia and Connecticut in the mid-1700s. At the time, the area was part of Luzerne County. As more and more people from Connecticut moved in, there began to be some conflict. Connecticut's original land grant gave it control of land within the northern and southern boundaries from present-day Connecticut to the Pacific Ocean. Their land grant overlapped with that of Pennsylvania. Soon fighting began between migrants from each state, resulting in the 1769–1799 [Pennamite–Yankee Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennamite%E2%80%93Yankee_War "Pennamite–Yankee War"). In the end, the government of Connecticut surrendered its claim on the area.

### Formation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Formation")]

In 1810, Susquehanna County was formed out of Luzerne County and later in 1812, Montrose was made the county seat.

### Coal and early prosperity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Coal and early prosperity")]

After the Civil War, coal started to be mined. Following this, railways and roads were built into the county allowing for more people to come. At one point the county had nearly 50,000 people. Coal became, as with neighboring counties, the backbone of the economy. This boom in coal would allow for an age of prosperity in the county.

### Great Depression

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Great Depression")]

When the Great Depression hit, the coal industry suffered horribly. Within months, the coal industry was struggling. During World War II, the coal industry picked up again, but only for a short time. Soon after, the economy in the county failed. Many mines were closed, railways were torn apart, and the economy took a turn for the worse. Unemployment rose and [population decline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_decline "Population decline") increased.[_[dubious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Accuracy\_dispute#Disputed\_statement "Wikipedia:Accuracy dispute")–[discuss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Susquehanna\_County,\_Pennsylvania#Dubious "Talk:Susquehanna County, Pennsylvania")_]

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Woman_with_display_at_Milk_Can_Corners%2C_Hallstead%2C_Pennsylvania%2C_1991.jpg/250px-Woman_with_display_at_Milk_Can_Corners%2C_Hallstead%2C_Pennsylvania%2C_1991.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Woman_with_display_at_Milk_Can_Corners,_Hallstead,_Pennsylvania,_1991.jpg)

Milk Can Corners in Hallstead

According to the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the county has a total area of 832 square miles (2,150 km 2), of which 823 square miles (2,130 km 2) is land and 8.7 square miles (23 km 2) (1.0%) is water.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-GR1-7)

Susquehanna County is very mountainous, with large concentrations of mountains in the east and smaller, more hill-like mountains in the west. The highest mountain in the county is North Knob just west of Union Dale. Most people live in one of the several long and mostly narrow valleys. These valleys are good farming land.

The county has a warm-summer [humid continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate") (_Dfb_) and average monthly temperatures in Montrose range from 21.2°F in January to 67.7°F in July.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-8)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the county had a population of 38,434. The median age was 48.2 years, 19.5% of residents were under the age of 18, and 23.7% of residents were 65 years of age or older; for every 100 females there were 100.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 99.6 males age 18 and over.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-Census2020DP-23)

The racial makeup of the county was 93.8% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans "White Americans"), 0.4% [Black or African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans"), 0.2% [American Indian and Alaska Native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"), 0.4% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Americans "Asian Americans"), <0.1% [Native Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Hawaiians "Native Hawaiians") and [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander "Pacific Islander"), 0.9% from some other race, and 4.3% from [two or more races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_Americans "Multiracial Americans"). [Hispanic or Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") residents of any race comprised 2.2% of the population.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-Census2020PL-24)

<0.1% of residents lived in urban areas, while 100.0% lived in rural areas.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-Census2020DHC-25)

There were 16,297 households in the county, of which 24.5% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 49.7% were married-couple households, 19.9% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 22.5% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 29.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 15.0% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-Census2020DP-23)

There were 21,259 housing units, of which 23.3% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 77.0% were owner-occupied and 23.0% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.7% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.3%.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-Census2020DP-23)

### 2000 census

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-GR8-26) of 2000, there were 42,238 people, 16,529 households, and 11,785 families residing in the county. There were 21,829 housing units at an average density of 26 units per square mile (10/km 2). The racial makeup of the county was 98.54% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.30% [Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)") or [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.15% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.22% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.01% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.17% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.60% from two or more races. 0.67% of the population were [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)") of any race. 26% were of [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_people "English people"), 16.1% were of [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_people "German people"), 15.1% [Irish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_people "Irish people"), 8.6% [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_people "Italian people") and 7.7% [Polish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_people "Polish people") ancestry.

There were 16,529 households, out of which 31.90% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 57.70% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 8.60% had a female householder with no husband present, and 28.70% were non-families. 24.30% of all households were made up of individuals, and 11.50% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.53 and the average family size was 2.99.

In the county, the population was spread out, with 25.50% under the age of 18, 6.70% from 18 to 24, 27.10% from 25 to 44, 25.20% from 45 to 64, and 15.50% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 40 years. For every 100 females, there were 98.90 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 95.80 males.

### Natural gas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Natural gas")]

Since unconventional drilling for natural gas began in 2008. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the unemployment rate in Susquehanna County was 6.1 percent in January 2008. It has since fluctuated between a high of 11.1 percent and a low of 3.1 percent. As of January 2018, the unemployment rate was 5.7 percent.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-43) After decades of population growth since the 1950s, the population in Susquehanna County has since begun to decline, concurrent with the expansion of natural gas drilling and accompanying infrastructure. Between 2010 and 2016, there was an estimated population decline of 5.8 percent. As of 2011, there were 1,079 active natural gas wells in the county which had collectively been issued 795 notices of violations by the Department of Environmental Protection of Pennsylvania.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-44)

### Rail

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Rail")]

Susquehanna County's last mainline passenger train services, through [New Milford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Milford,_Pennsylvania "New Milford, Pennsylvania") and [Hallstead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallstead,_Pennsylvania "Hallstead, Pennsylvania"), ended in January 1970. Since then, freight trains (presently [Norfolk Southern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk_Southern "Norfolk Southern")) use the railroad line.

### Air

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Air")]

Although Susquehanna County boasts several airstrips, they are strictly recreational. The closest main airports are in [Binghamton, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Binghamton_Airport "Greater Binghamton Airport") and [Scranton, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilkes-Barre/Scranton_International_Airport "Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport").

## Recreation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Recreation")]

There is one [Pennsylvania state park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pennsylvania_state_parks "List of Pennsylvania state parks") in Susquehanna County:

*   [Salt Springs State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Springs_State_Park "Salt Springs State Park") is 7 miles (11 km) north of [Montrose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montrose,_Pennsylvania "Montrose, Pennsylvania"), just off [Pennsylvania Route 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_Route_29 "Pennsylvania Route 29").

The Nature Conservancy manages two protected wildlife areas:

*   The [Woodbourne Forest and Wildlife Preserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodbourne_Forest_and_Wildlife_Preserve "Woodbourne Forest and Wildlife Preserve") is a 648 acres (262 ha) area located along Route 29 south of Montrose.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-46)
*   The _Florence Shelly Preserve_ is a 380 acres (150 ha) area located along Route 171 in Thompson Township.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-47)

There are nine properties/districts listed on [National Register of Historic Places in Susquehanna County, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places_listings_in_Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania "National Register of Historic Places listings in Susquehanna County, Pennsylvania")

**Susquehanna County** is a [county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States) "County (United States)") in the [Commonwealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_(U.S._state) "Commonwealth (U.S. state)") of [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the population was 38,434[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-QF-2) Its [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") is [Montrose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montrose,_Pennsylvania "Montrose, Pennsylvania").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-GR6-3) The county was created on February 21, 1810, from part of [Luzerne County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzerne_County,_Pennsylvania "Luzerne County, Pennsylvania")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-4) and later organized in 1812.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-5) It is named for the [Susquehanna River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_River "Susquehanna River"). The county is part of the [Northeast Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeastern_Pennsylvania "Northeastern Pennsylvania") region of the state.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-6)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Settlement and conflict

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Settlement and conflict")]

The first non-[Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_people "Indigenous people") settlers began to move into the area from Philadelphia and Connecticut in the mid-1700s. At the time, the area was part of Luzerne County. As more and more people from Connecticut moved in, there began to be some conflict. Connecticut's original land grant gave it control of land within the northern and southern boundaries from present-day Connecticut to the Pacific Ocean. Their land grant overlapped with that of Pennsylvania. Soon fighting began between migrants from each state, resulting in the 1769–1799 [Pennamite–Yankee Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennamite%E2%80%93Yankee_War "Pennamite–Yankee War"). In the end, the government of Connecticut surrendered its claim on the area.

### Formation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Formation")]

In 1810, Susquehanna County was formed out of Luzerne County and later in 1812, Montrose was made the county seat.

### Coal and early prosperity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Coal and early prosperity")]

After the Civil War, coal started to be mined. Following this, railways and roads were built into the county allowing for more people to come. At one point the county had nearly 50,000 people. Coal became, as with neighboring counties, the backbone of the economy. This boom in coal would allow for an age of prosperity in the county.

### Great Depression

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Great Depression")]

When the Great Depression hit, the coal industry suffered horribly. Within months, the coal industry was struggling. During World War II, the coal industry picked up again, but only for a short time. Soon after, the economy in the county failed. Many mines were closed, railways were torn apart, and the economy took a turn for the worse. Unemployment rose and [population decline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_decline "Population decline") increased.[_[dubious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Accuracy\_dispute#Disputed\_statement "Wikipedia:Accuracy dispute")–[discuss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Susquehanna\_County,\_Pennsylvania#Dubious "Talk:Susquehanna County, Pennsylvania")_]

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Woman_with_display_at_Milk_Can_Corners%2C_Hallstead%2C_Pennsylvania%2C_1991.jpg/250px-Woman_with_display_at_Milk_Can_Corners%2C_Hallstead%2C_Pennsylvania%2C_1991.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Woman_with_display_at_Milk_Can_Corners,_Hallstead,_Pennsylvania,_1991.jpg)

Milk Can Corners in Hallstead

According to the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the county has a total area of 832 square miles (2,150 km 2), of which 823 square miles (2,130 km 2) is land and 8.7 square miles (23 km 2) (1.0%) is water.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-GR1-7)

Susquehanna County is very mountainous, with large concentrations of mountains in the east and smaller, more hill-like mountains in the west. The highest mountain in the county is North Knob just west of Union Dale. Most people live in one of the several long and mostly narrow valleys. These valleys are good farming land.

The county has a warm-summer [humid continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate") (_Dfb_) and average monthly temperatures in Montrose range from 21.2°F in January to 67.7°F in July.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-8)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the county had a population of 38,434. The median age was 48.2 years, 19.5% of residents were under the age of 18, and 23.7% of residents were 65 years of age or older; for every 100 females there were 100.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 99.6 males age 18 and over.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-Census2020DP-23)

The racial makeup of the county was 93.8% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans "White Americans"), 0.4% [Black or African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans "African Americans"), 0.2% [American Indian and Alaska Native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"), 0.4% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_Americans "Asian Americans"), <0.1% [Native Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Hawaiians "Native Hawaiians") and [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander "Pacific Islander"), 0.9% from some other race, and 4.3% from [two or more races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_Americans "Multiracial Americans"). [Hispanic or Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") residents of any race comprised 2.2% of the population.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-Census2020PL-24)

<0.1% of residents lived in urban areas, while 100.0% lived in rural areas.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-Census2020DHC-25)

There were 16,297 households in the county, of which 24.5% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 49.7% were married-couple households, 19.9% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 22.5% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 29.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 15.0% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-Census2020DP-23)

There were 21,259 housing units, of which 23.3% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 77.0% were owner-occupied and 23.0% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.7% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.3%.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-Census2020DP-23)

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-GR8-26) of 2000, there were 42,238 people, 16,529 households, and 11,785 families residing in the county. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 51 people per square mile (20 people/km 2). There were 21,829 housing units at an average density of 26 units per square mile (10/km 2). The racial makeup of the county was 98.54% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.30% [Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)") or [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.15% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.22% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.01% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.17% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.60% from two or more races. 0.67% of the population were [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)") of any race. 26% were of [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_people "English people"), 16.1% were of [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_people "German people"), 15.1% [Irish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_people "Irish people"), 8.6% [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_people "Italian people") and 7.7% [Polish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_people "Polish people") ancestry.

There were 16,529 households, out of which 31.90% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 57.70% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 8.60% had a female householder with no husband present, and 28.70% were non-families. 24.30% of all households were made up of individuals, and 11.50% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.53 and the average family size was 2.99.

In the county, the population was spread out, with 25.50% under the age of 18, 6.70% from 18 to 24, 27.10% from 25 to 44, 25.20% from 45 to 64, and 15.50% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 40 years. For every 100 females, there were 98.90 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 95.80 males.

### Natural gas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Natural gas")]

Since unconventional drilling for natural gas began in 2008. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the unemployment rate in Susquehanna County was 6.1 percent in January 2008. It has since fluctuated between a high of 11.1 percent and a low of 3.1 percent. As of January 2018, the unemployment rate was 5.7 percent.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-43) After decades of population growth since the 1950s, the population in Susquehanna County has since begun to decline, concurrent with the expansion of natural gas drilling and accompanying infrastructure. Between 2010 and 2016, there was an estimated population decline of 5.8 percent. As of 2011, there were 1,079 active natural gas wells in the county which had collectively been issued 795 notices of violations by the Department of Environmental Protection of Pennsylvania.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-44)

### Rail

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Rail")]

Susquehanna County's last mainline passenger train services, through [New Milford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Milford,_Pennsylvania "New Milford, Pennsylvania") and [Hallstead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallstead,_Pennsylvania "Hallstead, Pennsylvania"), ended in January 1970. Since then, freight trains (presently [Norfolk Southern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk_Southern "Norfolk Southern")) use the railroad line.

### Air

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Air")]

Although Susquehanna County boasts several airstrips, they are strictly recreational. The closest main airports are in [Binghamton, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Binghamton_Airport "Greater Binghamton Airport") and [Scranton, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilkes-Barre/Scranton_International_Airport "Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport").

## Recreation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Recreation")]

There is one [Pennsylvania state park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pennsylvania_state_parks "List of Pennsylvania state parks") in Susquehanna County:

*   [Salt Springs State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Springs_State_Park "Salt Springs State Park") is 7 miles (11 km) north of [Montrose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montrose,_Pennsylvania "Montrose, Pennsylvania"), just off [Pennsylvania Route 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_Route_29 "Pennsylvania Route 29").

The Nature Conservancy manages two protected wildlife areas:

*   The [Woodbourne Forest and Wildlife Preserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodbourne_Forest_and_Wildlife_Preserve "Woodbourne Forest and Wildlife Preserve") is a 648 acres (262 ha) area located along Route 29 south of Montrose.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-46)
*   The _Florence Shelly Preserve_ is a 380 acres (150 ha) area located along Route 171 in Thompson Township.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania#cite_note-47)

There are nine properties/districts listed on [National Register of Historic Places in Susquehanna County, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places_listings_in_Susquehanna_County,_Pennsylvania "National Register of Historic Places listings in Susquehanna County, Pennsylvania")
